output.summary: A large shrub or small tree native primarily to California and southwestern Oregon, it often has several trunks and a broad, rounded crown. It leafs out very early, but inland plants commonly shed their leaves by late summer while coastal plants retain them longer. Native groups occasionally ate its poisonous seeds only after boiling and leaching them for several days, then grinding them into meal.
output.edibilityNote: Native groups occasionally ate seeds or nut meats after boiling and leaching toxins for several days, then grinding them into flour or meal.
